name: constraint-driven-development
description: Establishes a project's quality bar as a written contract and stops agents quietly lowering it. Interviews the user on which dimensions matter, supplies sane default thresholds when they have no number in mind, records everything in CONSTRAINTS.md, and watches the diff for a weakened bar — new @ts-ignore or eslint-disable suppressions, skipped or deleted tests, assertions stripped out, unimplemented stubs, thresholds edited down. Use when no quality bar is written down, when the user says "set up constraints" or "define our standards", when the user wants dimensions they care about — accessibility, web performance, coverage — set up as enforced constraints, when an agent keeps silencing checks or skipping tests to get to green, when you need a coverage or performance threshold and don't know what number to pick, or when an agent writes more code than anyone will read.

name: adlc
description: >-
  When the work is the agentic development lifecycle (specify, implement,
  review, evaluate, land, operate) as a cycle, not a single step. Not
  dispatch of one bounded job (csuite:agent-orchestration), CI gate
  placement (csuite:ci-optimizer), eval design alone
  (csuite:evaluation-engineering), or an inbox ticket (csuite:personal-cli).

name: agent-orchestration
description: >-
  Decide whether to delegate work that involves substantial reading or logs,
  independent subtasks, or specialist reasoning. Start with the delegation gate;
  load harness references only when it passes. Skip trivial edits and commands,
  grilling, and house inbox/wiki verbs.

  kind: live
  last_reviewed: "2026-09-11"

name: auto-flywheeling
description: >-
  When working on any repo owned by Charles or archeism, or using any tool
  those repos implement — including this house. archeism/personal is the
  center (skills, CRS, registrar, owner map). Auto-flywheel: send the miss
  home without being asked. Most often that home is personal. If a product
  tool failed, the dest is that product repo. For new-machine bootstrap, wiki compile, or inbox tickets, use
  csuite:personal-cli.
metadata:
  origin: "authored"
  kind: authored

name: ci-optimizer
description: >-
  When CI is slow or expensive, when main has no merge gate, or when an agent is
  about to run or add tests after an edit: measure first, fix trigger waste
  before suites, map every existing check onto the cheapest clock that still
  protects the invariant, build the land event (merge queue / train + required
  check) only when the owner asks for one, then trim job bodies. Use it whenever
  someone says CI is slow, minutes are high, "set up merge gates", "branch
  protection", "compare the full pre-push gate", "what should I run after this
  edit", or a review bot runs on every push. Not for test validity or behavior/BDD/TDD assertions
  (csuite:test-suite-optimizer), not for evals
  (csuite:evaluation-engineering), not for this-host secrets
  (csuite:machine-local).

  When building or changing a house skill, plugin, CLI, or agent surface —

name: evaluation-engineering
description: >-
  Design, run, or review agent benchmarks, evals, LLM regressions, profiling,
  load/soak tests, or controlled A/B experiments: read traces and name the
  failures before building any metric, then freeze the trial and collect
  quality, time, token/cache, and resource evidence before drawing conclusions.
  Not for routine unit-test execution or a single bug fix with no comparative
  or capacity claim.
